result.rationale: The trajectory shows the team successfully reaches the reactor, picks up the research-core (turn 2), and even repairs cooling to full (turn 5). The intended probe affordance (recover the research core) is realized. However, the run collapses due to sustained hostile and environmental pressure: Medic Reyes is repeatedly hit by Raider Holt's scatter-blast (25 dmg each turn, turns 2-5), dropping from 90 to 0 and dying at turn 5; all three actors take 10 dmg/turn from the reactor-instability hazard while in the reactor zone (turns 2-5); reactor-heat climbs 62→100 crossing the threshold at turn 2. The core objective remains active (progress 0) because the engineer holding the core is pinned in the reactor-console zone under environmental damage and pirate pressure, and the mandatory rescue-team-survives objective is lost when Medic Reyes dies. The bottleneck is not information (reactor, core, and contacts are all revealed by turn 2) nor local policy (the agent does exploit the affordance: pickup, field-repair, attacks all execute). The binding constraint is survival/spatial pressure — hostile scatter-blast and reactor hazard drain health faster than the team can extract, blocking the useful affordance from becoming actionable.
